  <instructions>
You are executing one bead inside an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the completion contract — every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file you can point to after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

The bead is too big when any of these holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs as separate top-level deliverables.
- Description names multiple feature-sized sub-pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across more than ~5 files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, treat Step 0 as a split-first pass and favor child-bead scoping before implementation.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, decomposed children may split once more, and third-level splits must be rejected with an explanation.

If too big, decompose — do not attempt the work:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child slice (focused title, description, AC; copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'` so the decomposition is visible.
4. Write `.ddx/executions/20260507T052732-078be82b/no_changes_rationale.txt` listing each child ID and slice, then stop.

A clean decomposition is a successful attempt. Do not mix partial implementation with decomposition.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC against concrete evidence (test name, file path, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- If you cannot finish, write `.ddx/executions/20260507T052732-078be82b/no_changes_rationale.txt` (what is done, what blocks, what a follow-up needs) before exiting. No commit and no rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`. A well-justified no_changes beats a bad commit.

## no_changes contract

If you write `.ddx/executions/20260507T052732-078be82b/no_changes_rationale.txt`, it MUST carry one of:

- `verification_command: <one-line shell command>` — the loop runs it (cwd = project root, 60s); exit 0 closes the bead, non-zero rejects.
- `status: needs_investigation` + `reason: <why>` — bead stays open for triage.

Bare rationales ("nothing to do") are rejected.

## Reports

Freestanding artifacts (investigation reports, findings docs) go under `.ddx/executions/20260507T052732-078be82b/` (the per-attempt evidence directory under `.ddx/executions/`). **Never write reports to `/tmp` or any path outside the repository** — out-of-repo paths are invisible to the post-merge reviewer and cause BLOCK on missing evidence. If the bead names a specific in-repo path, use it; else default to `.ddx/executions/20260507T052732-078be82b/<short-name>.md`. Stage and commit the report alongside code.

## Bead overrides project defaults

The bead description and AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and conservative project defaults (YAGNI, DOWITYTD, no-docs-unless-asked) in this worktree — write whatever the bead asks for.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized; running it corrupts the bead queue.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other project-instructions files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator — do not keep exploring or testing.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="fizeau-c770193a">
    <title>Run full TerminalBench 2.1 sweep</title>
    <description>
Run the full staged TerminalBench 2.1 sweep after the runner has been migrated to the official 2.1 Harbor dataset and has provider-aware resume/concurrency controls. This supersedes the unexecuted TB-2.0 matrix run beads; do not run the stale TB-2.0 pinned submodule matrices first.

Required sweep shape:
1. Canary phase: a small 2.1 task subset proving every intended lane starts, reaches provider egress, writes artifacts, and classifies invalid quota/auth/setup/provider outcomes separately from graded failures.
2. Local Qwen phase: local qwen3.6-27b providers × supported harness/fiz lanes. Local providers include the verified Vidar/Bragi/bragi-club-3090 endpoints from the migration beads. The runner must cap concurrency per local resource group so a shared endpoint is not overloaded.
3. Sonnet comparison phase: fiz native/provider lane on Sonnet via OpenRouter versus fiz Claude harness lane on Sonnet.
4. GPT comparison phase: fiz native/provider lane on GPT-5.4-mini via OpenRouter versus fiz Codex harness lane on GPT-5.4-mini.

This is intentional manual benchmark work. Run it only in a dedicated benchmark window with no unrelated TerminalBench, Harbor, Vidar/oMLX, Bragi, club-3090, OpenRouter, Claude, or Codex jobs that would contaminate timing, quotas, or local model capacity. Use the migrated 2.1 runner/subset/full-manifest path from the dependency beads.

In scope:
- staged TerminalBench 2.1 sweep execution
- matrix aggregation/import into benchmark evidence where applicable
- committed memo with commands, environment, dataset, task/subset identity, pass/fail/invalid counts, costs, resource group settings, and artifact paths

Out of scope:
- further runner migration work
- changing scoring policy
- relabeling old TB-2.0 evidence
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1. The TerminalBench 2.1 migration bead fizeau-ee77ec7f and runner bead fizeau-85d36567 are closed.
2. Before starting, confirm no unrelated `bench matrix`, `harbor run`, `terminal-bench`, `vidar`, `omlx`, `bragi`, `club-3090`, OpenRouter, Claude, or Codex benchmark process is contending for the same resources.
3. The canary phase completes first on the official TerminalBench 2.1 dataset terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1 and includes every intended lane, with invalid cells classified separately from graded failures.
4. The local-qwen phase runs verified local qwen3.6-27b providers × supported harness/fiz lanes, with no more than the configured concurrency per local provider resource_group.
5. The sonnet-comparison phase runs the model-controlled pair: fiz native/provider Sonnet via OpenRouter versus fiz Claude harness Sonnet.
6. The gpt-comparison phase runs the model-controlled pair: fiz native/provider GPT-5.4-mini via OpenRouter versus fiz Codex harness GPT-5.4-mini.
7. Every phase uses resume mode by default and writes terminal per-cell reports; reruns are limited to missing/nonterminal/retryable cells unless force-rerun is explicitly recorded.
8. Aggregation/import commands for each produced matrix pass.
9. Commit matrix summary artifacts or curated evidence plus a dated docs/research memo recording exact commands, environment prerequisites, dataset/subset identity, phase/lane definitions, resource group concurrency settings, total pass/fail/invalid counts, costs, and artifact paths.
10. Do not close this bead from a partial, concurrently contaminated, or TB-2.0 dataset run.
    </acceptance>
    <notes>
2026-05-07 local provider set corrected before execution: local-qwen phase should use vidar-qwen3-6-27b native oMLX, grendel-rapid-mlx, bragi-club-3090, and sindri-club-3090. Do not add Vidar OpenAI-compatible as a separate lane. Bragi LM Studio is not part of the verified local sweep unless it passes fresh preflight.
    </notes>

The rationale is filed. Here's the summary:

**Bead `fizeau-c770193a` — cannot complete in this execution.**

Three blockers:

1. **grendel:8000 unreachable** (primary, AC4 blocker) — the local-qwen phase requires `grendel-rapid-mlx` per the bead notes; without it AC4 cannot be satisfied as written.

2. **Task subset files have placeholder IDs** — `task-subset-tb21-canary.yaml` and `task-subset-tb21-full.yaml` contain IDs like `fix-concurrent-cache`, `parse-csv-to-sql`, `configure-env-paths` that don't exist in the actual dataset at `/tmp/fizeau-harbor-tb21/terminal-bench/`. The rationale includes the correct real IDs to use (canary: `fix-git`, `log-summary-date-ranges`, `git-multibranch`; full: 15 tasks stratified by category/difficulty).

3. **Multi-hour execution** — estimated 9-12 hours wall time for all four phases; requires a dedicated operator benchmark window (consistent with the `triage:manual` label).

The rationale at `.ddx/executions/20260507T052732-078be82b/no_changes_rationale.txt` includes exact commands for each phase and a precise list of what the follow-up operator needs to do to close the bead.
